owned_invariants: A graph is read only from a list of [u, v] pairs of exact integers; the list may be empty, and a loop or a second edge between two vertices is an edge like any other. Vertices are numbered in the order the edges first name them, and an edge runs from its first vertex to its second.
is_numbered holds exactly when the vertex names are 0 up to the vertex count less one, in any order.

forest is the breadth-first spanning forest that takes roots in vertex order and neighbours in edge order. Every vertex is reached once, a parent comes before its children in the order, and the edges outside the forest are the chords, in edge order.

fundamental_cycles gives one closed walk per chord, in chord order: the chord forwards, then the forest edges from its head up to where the two paths to the root meet, each against the way the forest climbs it, then the forest edges from its tail up to that point. Forest edges the two paths share are left out.

coboundary of a value on the vertices is, on each edge, the value at its head less the value at its tail. potential is zero at each root and matches the given edge values along the forest. residual is the edge values less the coboundary of a potential, and defect is the sum of the sizes of what the forest potential leaves.
defect is zero exactly when the edge values are a coboundary, which is exactly when their sum round every fundamental cycle is zero.
A list of values shorter than the edges or vertices it is read against is read as ending in zeros.
boundaries: The forest and its cycles are rebuilt on every call; nothing is cached. Callers bound the size of the graph.
Vertex numbers are positions in names(). Callers that speak in vertex names translate with vertex().
